problem: The question uses grep root /etc/passwd to produce the message 'Permission denied'. /etc/passwd is readable by every user, so grep on it will not print that error. A student may think grep itself raises the message, or may not see how the example could fail.
fix: Use a path that can really fail for an ordinary user, such as grep root /etc/shadow 2>&1 > hits.txt, or say plainly that the error line is coming from a file the user cannot read.

problem: The text says command substitution 'splits on spaces'. It actually splits on every character in IFS, which by default is space, tab and newline, and it also performs pathname expansion, so a name containing * or ? is expanded too. Calling it splitting on spaces only can make a student think tabs are safe.
fix: Write: unquoted command substitution is split on every IFS character (space, tab and newline) and then wildcards such as * are expanded, so a name like Ravi Kumar becomes two items, a blank line vanishes, and the whole file is loaded into memory first.
